steps.content: [Hourglass Effect]
The massive golden hourglass that symbolizes the rules of this world begins to move once more. You've lost count of how many times this has happened in this round, but it's reminding you to hurry up.
With Eleanor's hot spring inn guest list in hand, you quickly identify all residents with unconfirmed identities. The Clergyman crosses out the final name, a faint crease forming between his brows.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: Verification done. All registered guests have been confirmed.
All of them? Really? You stare silently at the page covered with crossed-out names.
After Eleanor leaves, you approach the Clergyman, whose brow is tightly furrowed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Everything that's happened today has at least made me certain of one thing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: When the game restarts, everyone revives, whether they're NPCs or players. If we include the Butcher currently sealed in the hot spring bath, that would indeed account for <color=#fb9259>everyone</color> you mentioned.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Except for one person. She has never appeared. No, perhaps you're deliberately avoiding mentioning her.
The Clergyman remains silent, fixing his gaze somewhere past your shoulder rather than meeting your eyes. Seeing his refusal to respond, you change your approach.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You once told me the Butcher's story, and explained how the Witch captures people's hearts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After the investigation into all players, I've come to understand something. The more deeply someone embraces their role in the story, the more meaning they find in their existence here. The roles the Witch creates for them are projections of what they desperately desire but cannot obtain in reality.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But Eleanor and I are different. We've only just entered this story and haven't yet found our roles. That's why we remain Voyagers, or Adventurers.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've come to understand all this thanks to your assistance. You are clear-headed and wise. These detailed records have helped me clarify crucial information, and I'm sincerely grateful to you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yet for this very reason, I'm all the more confused about your true thoughts...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>...Despite knowing the deceptive nature of this world, you don't seem anxious or eager to find a way out.</color>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've earned the "Clergyman" identity and play the role perfectly. Do you truly reject this world?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Or... have you also been captured by this game?
The Clergyman lowers his head and reaches up to loosen his tie. His shoulders relax, as if a heavy burden he's carried for a long time has finally been lifted.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: Yes... I am playing a role, and I'm enjoying it.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: Let me tell you another story, of someone else... In an office, he had no real name, only a nickname.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: Can you imagine? He had indeed chosen a convenient nickname, but five years later, all anyone ever said to him was still... "Hey, um, what's your name again? Glasses, come give us a hand."

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: They never remember he existed. They called him over when they needed him, then ignored him when they didn't... Well, that's modern society for you. Everyone's busy enough with their own lives. No point in burdening each other with expectations.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: So he learned to be cold, just like everyone else. He hid his emotions and gave up trying to express himself. No one cared about him, so he stopped caring about anyone in return.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: But here, it's different. People come to confess to him, address him as the Clergyman, look up to him, and depend on him. Even though it's all just fictional, it's the first time he's ever felt... that he matters.
He glances at you and adds candidly.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: ...You're right. Even knowing this is all just a game, I still want to stay.
You exhale slowly. Your extensive interrogation experience tells you the Clergyman isn't lying, so you decide to be honest in return.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ${PlayerName}. That's my real name. I'm the Chief of the MBCC, and this looping game we're in isn't just some immersive experience. It's a <color=#fb9259>Mania</color> incident caused by a <color=#fb9259>Sinner</color>.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I believe this entire scenario was constructed by the Witch using her Mania power. From the moment we stepped into that hot spring, we've entered her story. She created your Clergyman character to keep you tethered to this illusory satisfaction, just like the Butcher was controlled by his own ax. Everything we see is the Witch's doing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's tried to control me too. I can feel her watching me. Behind the terrifying illusions, between my countless deaths, her shadow has always been there.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Perhaps she's enjoying all this carnage, watching people go mad and slaughter each other. Hiding outside the narrative, mocking everything. But we won't let her have her way.
You take a deep breath.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I need you. Not the Clergyman from the story, but the real you!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've calmed my anxieties and offered support without being asked to. You've sensed my tension, and even empathized with the Butcher's inner struggles. A kind person like you deserves to be valued wherever you are. You've always been needed.
The Clergyman's shoulders tremble almost imperceptibly, and for the first time, a glimmer of light appears in his otherwise vacant eyes.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: "Kind"... Such a simple yet sincere compliment. It's been a long time since I've heard words like that. Thank you.

steps.speaker: Clergyman
steps.content: All right... I'll take you to find her.
